figures.alt: Commercial contractor qualification binder beside a blank insurance certificate and project notebook
figures.caption: Ask for the contractor license, insurance certificate, references, and scope documentation early. Qualification records should support the specific work being proposed.
figures.before: 1. They Can't Produce a License Number Immediately

figures.alt: Commercial planning table with abstract drawings, estimating tools, and a blank notebook
figures.caption: A written scope gives the owner a way to compare bids, exclusions, allowances, schedule expectations, and the actual work behind the price.
figures.before: 3. They Won't Provide a Written Scope of Work

figures.alt: Commercial renovation rough-in with exposed plumbing and electrical work beside a blank permit folder
figures.caption: Permits and inspections are field milestones, not paperwork to address after work starts. The project sequence should identify when each review will occur.
